# hardware/ — case, wiring, power

[← Main README](../README.md) · Firmware pins: [firmware/](../firmware/README.md)

The physical pendant: a **heart-shaped, two-part 3D-printed case** (≈ 58 × 54 × 17.6 mm closed) around the XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense and its LiPo, with a pulse-wave symbol engraved across the front — the vibe, the music, the heartbeat of the night. It hangs from a chain through an integrated bail loop at the top cleft. Modeling only for now; texture/finish comes at print time.

## Design (generated by [`3dprint/pendant.py`](3dprint/pendant.py))

- **`encore_body.stl`** — back shell (15 mm deep): heart cavity, **USB-C slot in the right lobe wall** (charge/flash without opening), **integrated bail ring** bridging the top cleft (chain hole front-to-back, Ø4.6), thumb notch at the tip to pry the lid.
- **`encore_lid.stl`** — front lid (5 mm): friction-fit lip (0.3 mm clearance), **pulse wave engraved 1.2 mm into the face** (prints face-down = crisp, and the thinned wall glows when the LED lights the inside), **3 mic holes** over the Sense PDM mic.
- **Rule (CLAUDE.md): never edit the STLs — edit `pendant.py` and regenerate.** Run it from inside `3dprint/` (`python pendant.py --render` also produces `fit_preview.png`). Needs `pip install trimesh shapely manifold3d numpy`.
- The generator **auto-sizes the heart** to the smallest shape whose cavity holds the components — change a component constant and the whole case re-fits.

## Component layout (the decision, baked into the generator)

**Stacked, not side-by-side**: the LiPo lies flat and horizontal across the widest band of the heart; the XIAO sits **on top of it** on foam tape, component side toward the lid, **USB-C edge against the right wall** (1 mm from the slot). Stacking gives the smallest face (58 mm heart); side-by-side would have needed a ~70 mm heart to clear the battery + board footprints. Stack height 10.7 mm vs 12.8 mm cavity depth — room above the board for the LED and wires.

**The header pins ("feet")**: they're breadboard headers, not fixings — nothing in the case uses them. **Clip them flush with side cutters** (the cavity assumes it): they'd otherwise add ~8 mm of depth and press into the battery pouch. Solder the three signal wires (touch → GPIO1, LED → GPIO2, plus 3V3/GND) into the through-holes from the top side — no desoldering needed. **The camera module unplugs** (lift the FPC latch); we only use the mic on the Sense board.

## Assembly

1. Battery in first, flat, wires exiting on the **left** side (dedicated slack space). The XIAO has no JST socket — cut the connector and solder the leads to the **BAT+/BAT− pads** under the board (mind polarity; the on-board circuit then charges via USB-C).
2. Foam tape on the battery, XIAO on top, USB-C aligned in the slot — test a cable before closing.
3. WS2812B (3V3/GND/DIN→GPIO2) taped inside, facing the lid so the engraving glows. Copper-tape touch pad inside the lid face, wire to GPIO1.
4. Lid on (pulse face out), pry open at the tip notch. Chain through the bail.

## Print settings (42 fablab / LabElec)

Transparent or translucent **PETG or PLA**, 0.2 mm layers, 2–3 perimeters, infill ≥ 25 %. **Body prints back-face down, lid prints pulse-face down** — no supports needed anywhere (the USB slot's 0.8 mm roof self-bridges). ~1h30 total. Light sanding inside the lid boosts the diffuse LED glow. Print one test lid first to check the friction fit (adjust `CLEAR` in `pendant.py` if too tight/loose).
